data.how-it-will-be-validated#How it will be: Area Criterion the table a table diff against NIST’s allascii.txt conversion factors within 1 ulp of the CODATA decimal SciPy’s scipy.constants (BSD-3-Clause) and astropy’s astropy.constants are the oracles. data.references#References: Subject Reference the values Mohr, Newell, Taylor and Tiesinga, Rev. Mod. Phys. 97 (2025), the CODATA recommended values the data source NIST’s ASCII table of the constants, public domain the SI BIPM, The International System of Units (SI Brochure)
data.what-it-will-provide#What it will provid: The CODATA 2022 recommended values: exact for h, e, k and N_A, and with their uncertainties, and the correlations, for the others. A Go table generated from NIST’s ASCII file by a reproducible tool in the repository, which records the edition. CODATA changes every four years, so the edition is data, not folklore.

data.how-it-will-be-validated#How it will be: Area Criterion dimensions exact rational dimension vectors conversion factors within 1 ulp of the decimal value in the references; a table diff against NIST SP 811 Oracles and references: pint (its definitions file is data that may be ported), astropy’s astropy.units, and UDUNITS-2 itself. The corpus is NIST Special Publication 811 and pint’s test suite. Every item also needs unit tests at 100% coverage and a performance table against the reference.

Rev. 4 (1914) 345, doi:10.1103/PhysRev.4.345 representation Hart, Multidimensional Analysis, Springer 1995, doi:10.1007/978-1-4612-4208-6
data.what-it-will-provide#What it will provid: A dimension vector of seven rational exponents, with a scale factor and an offset; the offset only for degC and degF. Quantities and conversion between compatible units. A parser for the UDUNITS grammar, which the CF conventions of NetCDF use, and a database of SI, US customary and derived units. Dimensional analysis: compatibility checks and Buckingham’s pi theorem, from the null space of the exponent matrix. In wave 4 (item 21), user-defined unit systems such as EMU, ESU and atomic units, as Maple’s Units package offers.
